chapter: Porgy and Bess and Varsity Show
title: The open fly and the boat-to-New York song
summary: Told his fly was open, he turns sideways to sing There's a Boat That's Leaving Soon for New York to Bess, and sings its lyrics.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: "All right, I leave it here Maybe you change your mind . . ." and the music plays and I make a turn and turn around and back up and go off.

But a little of the sense that happened just before that. Because as soon as I told her they're going to lock him up in jail and she don't want to take the happy dust and she pushes me, shoves me away and shoves me across the stage and when I get to the other side of the stage and one of the persons in the show says to me, "Your fly is open," and at that time they didn't have no zipper on the pants, had buttons. Ain't no way in the world for me to button those pants up, no way possible, not with one hand.

However, when they said that, I can't face the audience. What I have to do now is to do the song just the opposite. I got to turn my back to the audience, I got to go back across the stage to where Bess is by Porgy's

house and I got to put my right foot up on the stoop, put my right elbow on my knee to sing the song to Bess, both songs I'm going to sing to her. And when I start, do the step to go to her -- dee-dee-dee -- go sing the song to her, my right foot is up on the step and I got my chin in my hand looking at her, singing, and my right side is to the audience and I'm facing her. and I sing the song:
